Waller-Duncan k-ratio t test

Source: R/tests-extra.R
waller_duncan.Rd

Bayesian separation of the means of a treatment factor (Waller and Duncan 1969). Instead of a fixed significance level, the user gives the ratio K of the seriousness of a type I to a type II error; the critical t then adapts to the evidence of the analysis of variance: with a large F it approaches an unprotected LSD, with an F near 1 almost no difference is declared. The result is an "ad_comparison" object, so print(), plot() and plot_differences() work as with compare_means().

Usage

waller_duncan(fit, factor, K = 100, alpha = NULL)

Arguments

fit

An "ad_anova" object from design_anova().

factor

One treatment factor of fit.

K

Seriousness ratio of type I to type II errors (default 100).

alpha

Optional nominal level that sets K by the usual correspondence: 0.10 gives K = 50, 0.05 gives K = 100 and 0.01 gives K = 500. When NULL, the alpha reported is the comparison-wise error rate implied by the critical t.

Value

An object of class "ad_comparison" (see compare_means()), with the extra elements K, t_critical and F.

Details

The F, its degrees of freedom and the error come from the stratum that tests the factor in fit (for instance Error a for the main plots of a split-plot). With unequal replication every pair uses its own standard error, as in the Tukey-Kramer form.

References

Waller, R. A. and Duncan, D. B. (1969). A Bayes rule for the symmetric multiple comparisons problem. Journal of the American Statistical Association 64, 1484-1503.

See also

waller_critical(), compare_means()

Examples

fit <- design_anova(maize_nitrogen, "Yield_t_ha", "Nitrogen_kg_ha", block = "Block")
wd <- waller_duncan(fit, "Nitrogen_kg_ha")
wd
#> 
#> Waller-Duncan k-ratio t test (K = 100), alpha = 0.0672
#> Response: Yield_t_ha   compared: Nitrogen_kg_ha
#> Error: Residual error (MS = 0.01643, df = 9)
#> Bayesian k-ratio rule: K = 100, F = 437.3 on 3 and 9 df, critical t = 2.0803 (comparison-wise alpha about 0.067). 
#> Minimum significant difference = 0.1885
#> 
#>  Nitrogen_kg_ha n  mean      se raw_mean     sd group
#>             180 4 7.183 0.06409    7.183 0.2943     a
#>             120 4 6.885 0.06409    6.885 0.3663     b
#>              60 4 5.845 0.06409    5.845 0.2978     c
#>               0 4 4.215 0.06409    4.215 0.3101     d
#> 
#> Means sharing a letter do not differ.
plot(wd)
